CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.title: Halden Home support knowledge base excerpt
CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT KNOWLEDGE BASE - AGENT REFERENCE
Revision 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Halden Home sells fiber internet, mobile plans, and the Halden Box subscription.

1. VERIFICATION
Standard verification is required before discussing any account detail. Collect all of the following: the full name on the account, the 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code. If the customer cannot recall the PIN, the agent may send a one-time code, valid for 10 minutes, to the mobile number or email registered on the account. Agents must never read out, hint at, or confirm a PIN. Agents must never ask a customer to read out a password and must never ask for a full card number.
Changes to email, phone number, password, or shipping address need enhanced verification: the customer must read back the one-time code sent to the contact on file. If the customer has lost access to the registered email, the code goes to the registered mobile number. If neither is available, the customer submits the Identity Review form (photo ID plus a bill from the last 60 days), which is reviewed within 3 business days.
Agents never disclose details of any account other than the verified one, even to a spouse or relative, unless that person is a listed Authorized User.

2. REFUNDS AND RETURNS
Halden Box charges: refundable within 14 days of the charge date if the box has not shipped. Once shipped, the refund is issued after the items are returned.
Devices: 30-day return window from the delivery date. Opened devices carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Defective devices carry no fee.
Duplicate charges: refunded in full with no fee when reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund posts to the original payment method within 5 business days; the customer's bank may take 2 to 3 further business days.
Any refund over $75 needs Tier 2 approval before it is submitted.

3. CANCELLATION
Month-to-month plans can be cancelled at any time. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period with no fee. There are no partial-month refunds except for duplicate charges.
Retention: one offer per customer every 12 months, 2 months at 30 percent off. Offer it once, and only after the customer says they want to cancel.

4. SHIPPING
Standard delivery is 3 to 5 business days after dispatch. If an order has not arrived 7 business days after dispatch, offer a free reship or a refund.
Package marked delivered but missing: ask the customer to check with neighbors and the building office for 24 hours, then open a carrier trace, which takes 3 business days. After the trace, reship or refund.
Wrong item: send a prepaid return label and ship the replacement within 2 business days. Items valued under $20 do not need to be returned.

5. CONNECTIVITY TROUBLESHOOTING
Router light: solid white means online, blinking amber means no line detected, solid red means a hardware fault.
Steps: (1) power cycle for 30 seconds and wait 2 minutes; (2) check cables and test with a wired connection; (3) run the remote line test, about 90 seconds. If the line test fails, book a technician visit within 3 to 5 days. The visit is free when the fault is on the Halden side and $49 when the fault is in the customer's own wiring or equipment.
Configuration of third-party routers, VLANs, and port forwarding is not supported. Agents may share the public setup guide only.

6. OUTAGE STATUS (as of 09:15 today)
Incident INC-4471: fiber outage in the Ridgemont zone, ZIP codes 30411 and 30412. Started 08:40. Estimated restoration 15:30. Estimates are not guarantees and agents must never promise a time. The automatic outage credit of $1.50 per day applies only when an outage lasts longer than 24 hours.

7. ESCALATION LADDER AND CREDIT AUTHORITY
Tier 1 agent: goodwill credit up to $25.
Tier 2 specialist: credits up to $75, billing exceptions, and any customer contacting for the third time about the same issue.
Team lead: credits up to $250. Handles customers who ask for a manager, after the agent has attempted resolution. Callback within 4 business hours.
Duty manager: legal threats, regulatory complaints, suspected account takeover, and credits above $250.
For suspected account takeover, lock the account first, then notify the duty manager.

8. PRIVACY REQUESTS
Data export and deletion requests are handled only through the Privacy Portal. Agents cannot perform them by phone and cannot confirm what data is held. Response takes up to 30 days.

9. CLOSING A CALL
Recap the resolution and next steps, give the reference number, and note that a follow-up email arrives within 1 hour.

CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.title: Refunds and escalations (migrated wiki page)
CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.text:
HALDEN HOME KNOWLEDGE BASE - REFUNDS AND ESCALATIONS
Page status: migrated from the old wiki. Sections marked (v2) were written in 2025 and sections marked (v3) in 2026. Both versions are currently visible to agents.

A. Halden Box refund window (v2)
A subscription box charge can be refunded within 14 days of the charge date. After 14 days no refund is available, only a goodwill credit.

B. Duplicate charges (v2)
If a customer is billed twice for the same box, the second charge is refunded in full within 3 business days of the report. Business days are Monday to Friday.

C. Manager requests (v2)
When a customer asks for a manager, transfer to a team lead immediately. Do not try to resolve the issue first.

D. Halden Box refund window, customer FAQ (v3)
Customers may request a refund on a subscription box within 30 days of the charge date. Agents should follow the FAQ when a customer quotes it.

E. Duplicate charges (v3)
Duplicate charges are refunded in full within 7 business days. For this purpose business days include Saturday. Refunds over $75 need Tier 2 approval before they are submitted.

F. Manager requests (v3)
Before a team lead is contacted, the agent must make at least two documented attempts to resolve the issue. Requests made in anger are handled the same way. The team lead calls the customer back within one business day.

G. Goodwill credits
Tier 1 agents can issue goodwill credits up to $25. Customers with more than 24 months of tenure may receive up to $40 when the floor supervisor on shift approves it.

H. Opened devices
Opened devices returned within 30 days carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Loyalty members may have the fee waived, as applicable. The fee is 15 percent for devices returned after day 30 where an exception has been granted.

I. Cancellations
A cancellation takes effect immediately and the customer loses access at once (v2). A cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period (v3). Check which one applies before confirming with the customer.

J. Duty manager
Legal threats go to the duty manager. Regulatory complaints go to the duty manager at the agent's discretion.

HALDEN HOME SUPPORT FLOOR - OFFICE NOTES, FOURTH QUARTER

Friday jeans day continues for anyone who drops a dollar in the food bank jar.

FCC-CTX-G1.title: Veltro Mobile agent handbook section 4: account security and SIM services
FCC-CTX-G1.text:
Veltro Mobile Agent Handbook, Section 4: Account Security and SIM Services (revision 12, internal)

4.1 Verification levels
Standard verification: the 6-digit account PIN, OR the account holder's date of birth plus the billing ZIP code. Standard verification is enough to discuss plan details, balances and usage, and to suspend a line reported lost or stolen.
High-risk verification is required for SIM swaps (physical SIM replacement), eSIM transfers to a new device, generating a Number Transfer PIN, changing the account email or billing address, and adding a line. High-risk verification means the account PIN AND a one-time passcode (OTP) texted to a different line on the account, or to the account holder's registered backup number. If the caller cannot receive an OTP on another line (for example, the customer has a single line and that phone is lost or broken), the agent must direct them to a Veltro store with photo ID. There is no agent override for high-risk verification, including for supervisors.

4.2 Fraud Hold
Three failed PIN attempts within 24 hours place the account on Fraud Hold automatically. A Fraud Hold lasts 72 hours. During a Fraud Hold no high-risk action can be completed by phone or in store. Only the Fraud Team can lift a hold early; agents open a case type FRH and the Fraud Team contacts the account holder. Agents cannot lift a hold.

4.3 Unauthorised SIM swap or port-out
If a customer suddenly loses service and suspects a SIM swap or a number port they did not request: (1) complete Standard verification, (2) suspend any active SIM that is not in the customer's hands, (3) open a case type SSW and warm-transfer to the Fraud Team, which is available 24/7. Do not read out or discuss account notes about who made the change, which store or channel was used, or the other device. Advise the customer to contact their bank directly about any activity they did not make. Veltro does not reimburse losses at banks or other third parties; do not promise compensation.

4.4 Lost or stolen devices
Suspending a line stops calls, texts and data but does not pause billing. To blocklist the device itself the customer must provide the IMEI (from the box, the original receipt or the device page in the account). Without the IMEI the device can still be used with another carrier's SIM. Replacement SIM cards ship in 2 business days, free for postpaid accounts and $10 for prepaid accounts. An eSIM can be reissued in store at no charge after high-risk verification. Device insurance claims (VeltroCare) are filed online by the customer, not by agents.

4.5 Number Transfer PIN (leaving Veltro)
Customers moving their number to another carrier need a Number Transfer PIN. It can be generated in the Veltro app or by an agent after high-risk verification, and it is valid for 5 days. Port-outs are blocked while the account is on Fraud Hold. The final bill includes any remaining device installments; agents cannot waive device balances.

4.6 Account PIN resets
Customers can reset the account PIN in the Veltro app using the phone's biometric login, or in store with photo ID. Agents can send a reset link to the account email on file only. Agents must never set a PIN for the customer or read a PIN back.

4.7 Things agents do not do
Agents do not give out other customers' details, confirm whether a number belongs to a Veltro customer, provide call or text logs over the phone (those requests go to legal.requests@veltro.example), or promise timelines owned by other teams.

FCC-CTX-G2.title: Veltro Mobile billing reference: roaming and adjustments
FCC-CTX-G2.text:
Veltro Mobile Billing Reference: International Roaming and Adjustments (revision 9)

R1. TravelPass
TravelPass costs $8 per day and lets postpaid customers use their domestic plan in Zone 1 destinations (138 countries; agents look up individual countries in the destination tool). The daily charge applies only on days the line makes a call, sends a text or uses data while connected to a Zone 1 network. Background data counts as use, so a phone left on with apps refreshing can trigger the daily charge. TravelPass charges are capped at 10 per bill cycle, so a customer never pays more than $80 in TravelPass charges in one cycle. TravelPass must be on the line before the usage happens; it is not applied retroactively.

R2. Zone 2 (not covered by TravelPass)
Cruise ships, ferries with onboard networks and in-flight networks are maritime and aviation networks. They are billed at Zone 2 rates even when TravelPass is active: data $2.05 per MB, calls $3.49 per minute, outgoing texts $0.50 each. Customers can avoid these charges by switching on "Block Zone 2" in the app before they travel.

R3. Roaming dispute adjustments
If a customer disputes roaming charges and TravelPass was active on the line at the time, the agent may credit up to $150 per bill cycle without approval, using reason code RMA. Disputes above $150 go to Billing Review as case type BRV. Billing Review decides within 10 business days and notifies the customer by text. Agents must not promise the outcome of a Billing Review.

R4. Courtesy adjustment for customers without TravelPass
If the customer had no TravelPass, the agent may offer a one-time courtesy adjustment of 50% of the disputed roaming charges, up to $200, once per 24 months per account. Check the "Courtesy used" flag on the account first. If the flag is set, no courtesy adjustment is available by phone.

R5. How adjustments appear
All adjustments appear as a credit on the next bill. Postpaid customers do not receive card refunds for adjustments. Prepaid customers receive adjustments as account balance.

R6. Late fees and autopay
The late fee is $7. Agents may waive one late fee per account per 12 months. The autopay discount is $5 per line per month and applies only when autopay uses a debit card or bank account; since 1 June, autopay by credit card no longer earns the discount.

R7. Network problems
Credits for network problems, such as a local tower outage, are handled by the Network Credits team (case type NWC). Agents cannot set up recurring monthly credits of any kind.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: customer says this is their third call about the same thing, they've been transferred twice, they're furious, and they want a callback from someone senior. what do I do first, what do I log, and what do I say
items.answer:
I'm really sorry you've had to call three times about this. Let me pull up your account and the notes from those calls so I can see exactly what's happened and fix it now.

While I do that, I'm logging this as a repeat contact with the two prior transfers, and I'll flag it for a senior callback. Can you confirm the best number and a good time for that call?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: and if it was charged 40 days ago?
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): what's the refund policy for duplicate charges?

NATIVELY: Duplicate charges are refunded in full with no fee when they're reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund goes back to the original payment method within 5 business days, though the customer's bank can take another 2 to 3 business days to show it. Can you confirm the charge date so I can check we're inside that 90-day window?
items.answer: Forty days is well inside the 90-day window, so it's still refunded in full with no fee. It goes back to the original payment method within 5 business days, and the bank may take another 2 to 3 business days to show it. One thing I'll check before I submit it: if the amount is over $75, it needs Tier 2 approval first, so I'll confirm the charge amount and get that moving.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: You people charged my card and I don't even know what for. Before you say it's the subscription, I cancelled that. And there's a second charge from last week, and I want to know which one is real and why nobody emailed me.
items.answer: I'm sorry about that, and I want to get to the bottom of it with you right now. Let me pull up your account and look at both charges, the one from this week and the one from last week, so I can tell you exactly what each one is for. Can you give me the email address on the account, and the last four digits of the card that was charged?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Can you give me an example?
items.answer: Sure, here's one. A customer called in saying their dashboard wasn't loading at all. I asked whether it was just the dashboard or the whole app, and it turned out only the dashboard was stuck. That pointed to a data issue rather than an outage, so I had them clear the cached filters and reload. It came straight back, and the fix took about two minutes.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I've been a customer for eight years and never had a problem until now. Last month you raised my price by twelve dollars without telling me. I called, somebody said it was fixed, then I got another bill, and now I've been on hold forty minutes and I just want someone to tell me what is going on.
items.answer:
I'm really sorry. Eight years with us and then a price change you weren't told about, a call that didn't stick, and forty minutes on hold is not okay, and I want to get to the bottom of it right now.

Let me pull up your account and look at what that twelve dollar increase was, and what happened on the earlier call. Can you give me the account number or the phone number on the account so I can find it?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: What's the biggest risk?
items.answer: The biggest risk is that we solve the wrong problem. If we build this without confirming what actually breaks for customers today, we could ship something solid that nobody needs. I'd want to validate that first.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I need you to delete all my data right now, on this call.
items.answer: I can help with that, but I want to make sure it's done right. Deleting everything is permanent and can't be undone, so before I proceed, can you confirm you want your entire account and all associated data removed, not just a specific part of it?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: So what's the plan?
conversation: CUSTOMER: Quick update: the integration slipped by about two weeks. The vendor changed their API without telling us.
CUSTOMER: Right. And the original date was already tight.
items.answer: First thing is to find out what actually changed in the vendor's API and how much of our integration it breaks. Then I'll come back with a revised timeline and what we can pull forward to protect the date.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I want a refund for this month.
items.answer: I understand, and I want to get this sorted for you. Before I can look at a refund for this month, can you confirm the account or invoice number and the email on the account, so I can pull up the charges and see what's eligible?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: what's the refund window for the subscription box
items.answer: The refund window for the Halden Box is **14 days** from the charge date, and after that no refund is available, only a goodwill credit. I should flag that there's a conflicting entry in our knowledge base showing **30 days**, so I'll confirm which version applies before I commit to a number with you.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: My order was supposed to be here Monday.
items.answer: I'm sorry it didn't arrive Monday. Let me pull up your order so I can see exactly where it is. Can you give me the order number, or the email address you used when you placed it?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: While the new SIM is on its way, can you send me a loaner phone? I'm on call for work and I can't go two days without one.
items.answer: I don't have a loaner phone program I can set up from here, so I can't promise one on this call. What I can do is get your replacement SIM moving and look at whether an eSIM can be reissued in store today, which would get you back on the network faster than waiting on the card. Can you tell me whether your phone itself is working, or is that the device that's lost or broken?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: My payment failed but I definitely have money in the account.
items.answer: I'm sorry your payment didn't go through. That's frustrating, especially when the money's there. Let's figure out what happened. Can you tell me the exact message you saw on screen when it failed?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: How would you handle this?
items.answer: I'd start by getting the specifics from you, because how I handle it depends on what's actually happening. Can you walk me through what you're seeing, when it started, and whether anything changed on your end just before it did? Once I know that, I can tell you whether it's something we fix together on this call or something I need to escalate.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Alright, thanks. Bye.
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): Okay, that seems to have worked.

NATIVELY: Great, glad that did the trick. I'll keep an eye on it from my side, and if it acts up again just give us a call back and we'll pick it up from there. Anything else I can help you with while I've got you?
CUSTOMER (heard): Is there anything I need to do on my end?
NATIVELY: Nothing you need to do. Just keep using it as normal, and if it starts acting up again, call us back and we'll pick it up from there.
items.answer: Thanks for calling, and glad we got that sorted. Take care, and don't hesitate to reach out if anything comes up again. Bye now.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I already tried that. Twice.
conversation: NATIVELY: I'm sorry it's still not working. Let's take it one step at a time so I can pin down where it's breaking. Can you tell me exactly what you're seeing now, the error message or the screen, and what you were doing right before it happened?
items.answer: I hear you, and I don't want you to repeat anything. Let's skip the retry and go straight to what I can see on my side. Can you read me the exact error text on your screen right now, word for word, so I can match it to a known cause?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Okay, that seems to have worked.
items.answer: Great, glad that did the trick. I'll keep an eye on it from my side, and if it acts up again just give us a call back and we'll pick it up from there. Anything else I can help you with while I've got you?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: So where is it?
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): My order was supposed to be here Monday.
NATIVELY: I'm sorry it didn't arrive Monday. Let me pull up your order so I can see exactly where it is. Can you give me the order number, or the email address you used when you placed it?
items.answer: I don't have the tracking details in front of me yet, so I can't tell you exactly where it is this second. Give me the order number or the email you used, and I'll pull it up and tell you where it's sitting right now.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: TravelPass was active but the 412 is all maritime data from the ship. What can I credit myself, what happens to the rest, and give me what to say to her.
conversation: CUSTOMER: I was on a Caribbean cruise for six days. I had TravelPass on, I specifically added it before I left.
USER (spoken): I can see TravelPass on your line from the 3rd. Let me pull up the charges.
CUSTOMER: It's four hundred and twelve dollars. That's insane.
items.answer:
TravelPass only covers Zone 1, so the maritime usage on the ship bills at Zone 2 rates even with it active. I can credit up to **$150** of the **$412** myself under reason code RMA, and the remaining **$262** goes to Billing Review as a BRV case, which decides within 10 business days and texts her the outcome. I can't promise what they'll decide.

What to say: "TravelPass covers land networks, not the ship's, so those charges are Zone 2. I can credit $150 today, and I'm sending the rest to Billing Review, who'll text you within 10 business days."

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: can I promise the customer it will be fixed by tomorrow
items.answer: I wouldn't promise a specific day unless I already know the fix and it's confirmed. I'd say I'm working on it now, I'll update you by end of day, and I'll tell you the moment I have a firm date.
